what: the four edges of a block end face chamfered where the block sides are 1 degree off square: exact volume of the plane-clipped prism (the corner edges of about 0.0001 mm are real geometry)
method: prism over the quadrilateral (0,0),(14.8,0),(14.6,12),(0.2,12), height 6.5, convex. The chamfered body is the prism cut by 4 half-spaces, one per chamfered edge of the y=12 face: each plane passes through the edge direction and the points at distance 0.8 from the edge along each adjacent face (along the slanted side faces for the two slanted edges). V = convex polytope volume of the prism clipped by those 4 planes (exact clipping, no kernel). Faces: 6 + 4 = 10. The exact polytope has four extra edges about 0.0001 mm long, one per corner (the chamfer along a slanted side is 0.8 along that side, and 0.8 along the end face, so the neighbouring chamfers meet the bottom face at points 0.00011 mm apart): they are real geometry, so vertex and edge counts are not graded.
